source_title: Atari Officially Shutting Down Gaming Platform - GameRant
source_excerpt:
Atari has announced plans to close its Atari VCS store soon and end support for the console. Released in 2021, the Atari VCS is a PC-console hybrid that can play many classic games. Atari marketed it as a modernized version of the Atari 2600, which was originally called the Video Computer System.
The VCS faced a rocky road before reaching production. Atari tried to boost interest with new game releases but ultimately seemed unhappy with its sales. Some even believed the VCS contributed to the company's major financial losses in 2021 and 2022 ( via Time Extension ). Still, many fans of Atari's retro games loved the console and saw it as a welcome addition to their collections, despite its hefty $399.99 price tag.
Atari to Shut Down the VCS Store in February 2027
On October 21, 2026, Atari announced that it had "stopped onboarding new games, and [it] will be shutting down the Atari VCS software store early next year." The shutdown will take place on February 1, 2027 , and the announcement also means the console will no longer receive firmware updates. That said, Atari seems to have plans to help current owners continue playing their classic games and discover new titles after the shutdown.

According to Atari, an upcoming OS update will remove the VCS's reliance on the company's infrastructure, allowing users to run their retro games offline. Meanwhile, Atari plans to release its Home Brew app on all VCS devices , allowing owners to discover new titles. Atari says, "[the Home Brew app] will allow everyone to add new games to your VCS independently, so developers can continue to build apps for the VCS and share them with the community." In the coming weeks, the company will release detailed guides to help users prepare to migrate their games to the console.

The VCS came with more than 100 built-in games from Atari's extensive library . Players could also buy more classic games through the console's namesake software store. The shutdown won't cut off access to games users already own , as they will still be able to play them offline. However, the official store will soon stop offering games for purchase, leaving console owners with home-brew games as their only way to add new titles.
Without explaining the decision, Atari said, "We took what was planned as a one-off Kickstarter program and turned it into a platform that we have collectively supported since 2020." However, some would argue that roughly six years of support can fall short of consumer expectations. Atari has acknowledged that the news may raise questions among current VCS owners and offered additional support through its Discord servers.
Users will be able to continue purchasing new games on the Atari VCS storefront through January 31, 2027.
